title: Hong Shao Rou
subtitle: Chinese red-braised pork belly
excerpt: Red-braised pork belly is one of the great achievements of Chinese home cooking. Long, slow braising in soy, aromatics and a touch of honey turns fatty pork into something tremblingly tender with a deep lacquered sauce.
sourceNotes: Hong shao rou originates in Hunan and Zhejiang provinces and is said to have been a favourite of Chairman Mao. Each region has its own version; the Shanghainese variety uses more sugar, while Hunan versions have more chilli.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in the braising liquid for up to 3 months. Reheat gently from frozen with a splash of water.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Even better made the day before. Refrigerate overnight and lift off any solidified fat before reheating.

content.text: The initial blanching step removes impurities and prevents the sauce from becoming muddy. Do not skip it.
Place the pork belly pieces in a pot of cold water and bring to a boil. Cook for 5 minutes, then drain and rinse.
Return the blanched pork to the pot with 500ml of fresh water. Add the dark soy, light soy, mirin, star anise, cinnamon, cloves, ginger and garlic.
Bring to a boil, then reduce to a very low simmer. Cover and cook for 60 minutes, turning the pork every 20 minutes.
Add the honey and stir to combine. Remove the lid and increase the heat to medium. Cook for a further 20 minutes, turning the pork frequently, until the sauce is thick and glossy and coats the pork.
Remove the whole spices and serve with steamed rice and greens.

items.symptom: Sauce has burnt on the bottom of the pan.
items.cause: Heat was too high during the uncovered reduction stage.
items.fix: Keep to a moderate bubble and stir every few minutes.

items.symptom: Pork is still tough after 60 minutes.
items.cause: The simmer was too vigorous and dried out the braise.
items.fix: Add a splash of water and continue on the lowest heat.
